text: OmopMultistate estimates individuals move clinically meaningful states time using cohort records OMOP Common Data Model. state represented cohort definition, transition matrix declares movements states possible. package provides workflow : prepare OMOP cohort_table long format used mstate; estimate state occupation probabilities overall specific initial states; repeat analysis across user-defined strata; return results standard summarised_result object visualise time.

title: Multi-State Analyses Using the OMOP Common Data Model
text: following example models acetaminophen treatment, discontinuation, restarting treatment, death absorbing state. uses synthetic synpuf-1k dataset, omock downloads first use, temporary DuckDB database. example requires omock, CohortConstructor, CodelistGenerator, CDMConnector, duckdb; plotting also requires visOmopResults, ggplot2, scales. function help pages provide smaller examples using bundled GiBleed dataset model first discontinuation, untreated absorbing. examples run locally without dataset download database connection. use CohortConstructor create three cohorts: acetaminophen treatment, discontinuation (untreated), death (death_cohort). Cohort names must match state names transition matrix. Cohort start dates mark state entries; reaching cohort end date alone create state change, construct discontinuation explicitly. Requiring day treatment end within observation prevents loss follow-counted discontinuation. permitted transitions : acetaminophen untreated acetaminophen death_cohort untreated acetaminophen untreated death_cohort Rows describe state left columns describe destination. NA entry forbids transition; row containing NA makes state absorbing. records can occur date. resolve ties logical order, placing death last absorbing state. default, stateStep = 0.01 separates successive priority ranks hundredths day. Without hierarchy, simultaneous competing states cause error. person’s time zero first entry state outgoing transition. , first recorded treatment discontinuation. Follow-ends observation end default. supplied censorDate column replaces default, missing dates falling back observation end; custom dates automatically capped observation end. Use consistent endpoint across person’s state records administrative censor date. can prepare data long format used mstate fit models: Tstart Tstop days since time zero. status = 1 identifies observed transition; possible transitions interval status = 0. estimate state occupation probabilities, use summariseMultistateProbabilities(). followUpDays argument limits time points returned fitting; use censorDate change input follow-endpoint. run interactively, functions can print informational (ℹ) messages records excluded. example, person death record never enters eligible initial state contribute analysis. messages describe input data; R warnings. tidy(), variable_name identifies destination state (example, prob_untreated), variable_level contains elapsed days character values, probability proportion zero one. initial_state gives state probabilities conditioned. initial_state = "overall" weights state-specific estimates observed starting-state distribution. settings(result) records analysis settings, including transition structure. Probabilities returned model time points rather every day. row exactly followUpDays guaranteed. can visualise now results. States displayed order appear transition matrix:
code: library(OmopMultistate) library(omock) library(CohortConstructor) library(CodelistGenerator) library(dplyr)  cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "synpuf-1k", source = "duckdb")  cdm codes <- getDrugIngredientCodes(cdm = cdm, name = "acetaminophen", nameStyle = "{concept_name}")  # acetaminophen cohort cdm$acetaminophen <- conceptCohort(cdm = cdm, conceptSet = codes, name = "acetaminophen") #> ℹ Subsetting table drug_exposure using 6620 concepts with domain: drug. #> ℹ Combining tables. #> ℹ Creating cohort attributes. #> ℹ Applying cohort requirements. #> ℹ Merging overlapping records. #> ✔ Cohort acetaminophen created.  # death cohort cdm$death_cohort <- deathCohort(cdm = cdm, name = "death_cohort") #> ℹ Applying cohort requirements. #> ✔ Cohort death_cohort created.  # untreated cohort cdm$untreated <- cdm$acetaminophen |>   padCohortEnd(days = 1L, requireFullContribution = TRUE, name = "untreated") |>   padCohortDate(days = 0L, indexDate = "cohort_end_date", cohortDate = "cohort_start_date") |>   renameCohort("untreated")  # bind them together cdm <- bind(cdm$acetaminophen, cdm$death_cohort, cdm$untreated, name = "my_study")  # the created cohort settings(cdm$my_study) #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   cohort_definition_id cohort_name   cdm_version vocabulary_version #>                  <int> <chr>         <chr>       <chr> #> 1                    1 acetaminophen 5.4         v5.0 29-APR-16 #> 2                    2 death_cohort  <NA>        <NA> #> 3                    3 untreated     5.4         v5.0 29-APR-16 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: subset_cohort_table <chr>, subset_cohort_id <chr> trans <- transMat(   x = list(c(2, 3), c(1, 3), c()),   names = c("acetaminophen", "untreated", "death_cohort") )  trans #>                to #> from            acetaminophen untreated death_cohort #>   acetaminophen            NA         1            2 #>   untreated                 3        NA            4 #>   death_cohort             NA        NA           NA stateHierarchy <- c("acetaminophen", "untreated", "death_cohort") msData <- prepareMultistateData(   cohort = cdm$my_study,   trans = trans,   stateHierarchy = stateHierarchy )  msData |>   arrange(subject_id, Tstart) |>   head(10) #> An object of class 'msdata' #> #> Data: #>    subject_id from to trans Tstart Tstop status     from_name       to_name #> 1           1    1  2     1      0    30      1 acetaminophen     untreated #> 2           1    1  3     2      0    30      0 acetaminophen  death_cohort #> 3           1    2  1     3     30   373      1     untreated acetaminophen #> 4           1    2  3     4     30   373      0     untreated  death_cohort #> 5           1    1  2     1    373   403      1 acetaminophen     untreated #> 6           1    1  3     2    373   403      0 acetaminophen  death_cohort #> 7           1    2  1     3    403   532      1     untreated acetaminophen #> 8           1    2  3     4    403   532      0     untreated  death_cohort #> 9           1    1  2     1    532   552      1 acetaminophen     untreated #> 10          1    1  3     2    532   552      0 acetaminophen  death_cohort result <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(   cohort = cdm$my_study,   trans = trans,   stateHierarchy = stateHierarchy ) tidy(result) |>   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   cdm_name  initial_state variable_name      variable_level probability #>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr>              <chr>                <dbl> #> 1 synpuf-1k overall       prob_acetaminophen 0                    1 #> 2 synpuf-1k overall       prob_untreated     0                    0 #> 3 synpuf-1k overall       prob_death_cohort  0                    0 #> 4 synpuf-1k overall       prob_acetaminophen 10                   0.770 #> 5 synpuf-1k overall       prob_untreated     10                   0.230 #> 6 synpuf-1k overall       prob_death_cohort  10                   0 #> # ℹ 5 more variables: cohort_table_name <chr>, follow_up_days <chr>, #> #   state_hierarchy <chr>, state_step <chr>, transitions <chr> result |>   filterGroup(initial_state == "acetaminophen") |>   plotMultistateProbabilities()

title: Multi-State Analyses Using the OMOP Common Data Model
text: Add columns constant within person requesting strata. following fits models sex well unstratified model: Use strata = list("sex", c("sex", "age_group")) age_group column also present request sex-specific joint sex age models. Missing strata values labelled "Missing". value "overall" strata column identifies result pooled across variable. model fitted stratum, informational message explains error stratum contributes probability rows. Filtering filterStrata(sex == "overall") selects unstratified model. Passing several strata plotMultistateProbabilities() creates separate panels; timeScale = "years" converts x-axis days years.
code: cdm$my_study <- PatientProfiles::addSex(cdm$my_study) bySex <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(   cohort = cdm$my_study,   trans = trans,   strata = list("sex"),   followUpDays = 365,   stateHierarchy = stateHierarchy )  bySex |>   filterGroup(initial_state == "acetaminophen") |>   filterStrata(sex == "Female") |>   tidy() |>   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   cdm_name  initial_state sex    variable_name      variable_level probability #>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr>  <chr>              <chr>                <dbl> #> 1 synpuf-1k acetaminophen Female prob_acetaminophen 0                    1 #> 2 synpuf-1k acetaminophen Female prob_untreated     0                    0 #> 3 synpuf-1k acetaminophen Female prob_death_cohort  0                    0 #> 4 synpuf-1k acetaminophen Female prob_acetaminophen 10                   0.746 #> 5 synpuf-1k acetaminophen Female prob_untreated     10                   0.254 #> 6 synpuf-1k acetaminophen Female prob_death_cohort  10                   0 #> # ℹ 4 more variables: follow_up_days <chr>, state_hierarchy <chr>, #> #   state_step <chr>, transitions <chr>

title: Plot Multi-State Occupation Probabilities — plotMultistateProbabilities
code: library(CohortConstructor) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’ #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’: #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’: #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union library(omock) library(OmopMultistate)  cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed") #> ℹ Loading bundled GiBleed tables from package data. #> ℹ Adding drug_strength table. #> ℹ Creating local <cdm_reference> object.  # An illustrative concept set: aspirin 81 mg oral tablets. # Keep the first treatment episode for each person. cdm$treated <- conceptCohort(   cdm = cdm,   conceptSet = list(treated = 19059056L),   name = "treated" ) |>   requireIsFirstEntry() #> ℹ Subsetting table drug_exposure using 1 concept with domain: drug. #> ℹ Combining tables. #> ℹ Creating cohort attributes. #> ℹ Applying cohort requirements. #> ℹ Merging overlapping records. #> ✔ Cohort treated created.  # Enter the untreated state the day after treatment ends. Require that day # to be within observation, so loss to follow-up is not a discontinuation. cdm$untreated <- cdm$treated |>   padCohortEnd(days = 1L, requireFullContribution = TRUE, name = "untreated") |>   padCohortDate(     days = 0L, indexDate = "cohort_end_date", cohortDate = "cohort_start_date"   ) |>   renameCohort("untreated") cdm <- bind(cdm$treated, cdm$untreated, name = "states")  # Model first discontinuation: untreated is an absorbing state. # Matrix state names must match the cohort names. trans <- transMat(   x = list(2, integer()),   names = c("treated", "untreated") )  cdm$states <- PatientProfiles::addSex(cdm$states) result <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(   cohort = cdm$states,   trans = trans,   strata = list("sex"),   followUpDays = 365,   stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated") ) #> `cohort_table_name` eliminated from settings as all elements are NA.  # Show the overall probabilities for people starting treatment. result |>   filterGroup(initial_state == "treated") |>   filterStrata(sex == "overall") |>   plotMultistateProbabilities()   # Compare the sex strata in separate panels, with time displayed in years. result |>   filterGroup(initial_state == "treated") |>   filterStrata(sex != "overall") |>   plotMultistateProbabilities(timeScale = "years")   cdmDisconnect(cdm)

title: Prepare Multi-State Data from an OMOP Cohort Table — prepareMultistateData
text: cohort cohort_table object containing one cohort state multi-state model. Cohort names must match state names trans. trans Transition matrix describing states transitions multi-state model. S number states multi-state model, trans S x S matrix, (,j)-element positive integer transition j possible multi-state model, NA otherwise. particular, diagonal elements NA. integers indicating possible transitions multi-state model sequentially numbered, 1,...,K, K number transitions. Row column names must identical, unique state names order. row containing NA defines absorbing state. Use transMat() build matrix. eventDate Name date column cohort identifies individual enters state. State entries defined dates; reaching cohort_end_date automatically create state change. censorDate Name date column cohort identifies end follow-, inclusive. NULL, end individual's observation period used. Missing values supplied column also fall back observation period end. Supplied dates replace observation-based dates; automatically capped observation end. Use date state records person specifying single follow-endpoint. stateHierarchy Character vector state names order used resolve states occur date, earlier entries occurring first. empty character vector applies hierarchy; unresolved ties competing states cause error. Include states need distinct order. Unlisted states share priority last listed state. stateStep Numeric increment used separate states occur date according stateHierarchy, days. Successive priority ranks shifted multiples increment. default 0.01 days.

title: Prepare Multi-State Data from an OMOP Cohort Table — prepareMultistateData
text: Time zero person's earliest entry state least one outgoing transition. People recorded absorbing states enter analysis. step, earliest subsequent entry permitted trans determines next state. Repeated visits supported matrix permits returning previous state. Cohort end dates alone create exits; provide cohort destination state. Events censor date included. records beyond censor dates removed, latest remaining censor date person used trajectory. stateHierarchy shifts -day event beyond date, follow-extended include shifted event. Informational messages report excluded records: events censoring, people without eligible initial state, events time zero, states reached trans. Counts refer records, rather distinct people. Remaining simultaneous competing states cause error; use stateHierarchy order . State records collected R processing, including cohort stored database.

title: Prepare Multi-State Data from an OMOP Cohort Table — prepareMultistateData
code: library(CohortConstructor) library(dplyr) library(omock) library(OmopMultistate)  cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed") #> ℹ Loading bundled GiBleed tables from package data. #> ℹ Adding drug_strength table. #> ℹ Creating local <cdm_reference> object.  # An illustrative concept set: aspirin 81 mg oral tablets. # Keep the first treatment episode for each person. cdm$treated <- conceptCohort(   cdm = cdm,   conceptSet = list(treated = 19059056L),   name = "treated" ) |>   requireIsFirstEntry() #> ℹ Subsetting table drug_exposure using 1 concept with domain: drug. #> ℹ Combining tables. #> ℹ Creating cohort attributes. #> ℹ Applying cohort requirements. #> ℹ Merging overlapping records. #> ✔ Cohort treated created.  # Enter the untreated state the day after treatment ends. Require that day # to be within observation, so loss to follow-up is not a discontinuation. cdm$untreated <- cdm$treated |>   padCohortEnd(days = 1L, requireFullContribution = TRUE, name = "untreated") |>   padCohortDate(     days = 0L,     indexDate = "cohort_end_date",     cohortDate = "cohort_start_date"   ) |>   renameCohort("untreated") cdm <- bind(cdm$treated, cdm$untreated, name = "states")  # Model first discontinuation: untreated is an absorbing state. # Matrix state names must match the cohort names. trans <- transMat(   x = list(2, integer()),   names = c("treated", "untreated") )  # By default, follow-up ends at the end of each person's observation period. # Resolve any same-day states by placing treatment before discontinuation. msData <- prepareMultistateData(   cohort = cdm$states,   trans = trans,   stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated") )  # One row per possible transition and time interval; status = 1 is an event. msData |>   arrange(subject_id, Tstart) |>   head() #> An object of class 'msdata' #>  #> Data: #>   subject_id from to trans Tstart Tstop status from_name   to_name #> 1          1    1  2     1      0    29      1   treated untreated #> 2          2    1  2     1      0    15      1   treated untreated #> 3          3    1  2     1      0    22      1   treated untreated #> 4          5    1  2     1      0    68      1   treated untreated #> 5          6    1  2     1      0    15      1   treated untreated #> 6          7    1  2     1      0    15      1   treated untreated  cdmDisconnect(cdm)

title: Summarise Multi-State Occupation Probabilities over time — summariseMultistateProbabilities
text: cohort cohort_table object containing one cohort state multi-state model. Cohort names must match state names trans. trans Transition matrix describing states transitions multi-state model. S number states multi-state model, trans S x S matrix, (,j)-element positive integer transition j possible multi-state model, NA otherwise. particular, diagonal elements NA. integers indicating possible transitions multi-state model sequentially numbered, 1,...,K, K number transitions. Row column names must identical, unique state names order. row containing NA defines absorbing state. Use transMat() build matrix. strata List character vectors defining stratifications. character vector identifies one columns cohort; separate model fitted combination values. example, list("sex", c("sex", "age_group")) requests models sex sex age group jointly. unstratified model always included. column must constant within person across cohort records. Missing values labelled "Missing". followUpDays Maximum number days follow-estimate state occupation probabilities. Use Inf include available follow-. limits time points returned model fitting; censor input data refit model horizon. eventDate Name date column cohort identifies individual enters state. State entries defined dates; reaching cohort_end_date automatically create state change. censorDate Name date column cohort identifies end follow-, inclusive. NULL, end individual's observation period used. Missing values supplied column also fall back observation period end. Supplied dates replace observation-based dates; automatically capped observation end. Use date state records person specifying single follow-endpoint. stateHierarchy Character vector state names order used resolve states occur date, earlier entries occurring first. empty character vector applies hierarchy; unresolved ties competing states cause error. Include states need distinct order. Unlisted states share priority last listed state. stateStep Numeric increment used separate states occur date according stateHierarchy, days. Successive priority ranks shifted multiples increment. default 0.01 days.

title: Summarise Multi-State Occupation Probabilities over time — summariseMultistateProbabilities
text: summarised_result result type "summarise_multistate_probabilities". Use tidy() obtain columns: initial_state: conditioning state, "overall" weighted estimate; variable_name: "prob_" followed destination state name; variable_level: elapsed days since time zero, stored character; probability: state occupation probability scale zero one; requested strata columns, "overall" unstratified results. settings() contains analysis settings, including permitted transitions follow-horizon. ms_data attribute contains prepared data used fitting, requested strata columns.

title: Summarise Multi-State Occupation Probabilities over time — summariseMultistateProbabilities
text: model uses survival::coxph() separate baseline hazard transition, clustering person, Breslow handling tied event times. mstate::msfit() mstate::probtrans() estimate state occupation probabilities time zero. Time zero, censoring, exclusions follow prepareMultistateData(). Results provided conditional initial state, together overall estimate weighted observed distribution initial states model's population. strata requested, repeated within stratum, alongside unstratified analysis. fitting fails stratum, informational message identifies underlying error; stratum contributes probability rows. Time points returned fitted model, including time zero, restricted followUpDays. row exactly followUpDays guaranteed. Confidence intervals included returned result.

title: Summarise Multi-State Occupation Probabilities over time — summariseMultistateProbabilities
code: library(CohortConstructor) library(dplyr) library(omock) library(OmopMultistate)  cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed") #> ℹ Loading bundled GiBleed tables from package data. #> ℹ Adding drug_strength table. #> ℹ Creating local <cdm_reference> object.  # An illustrative concept set: aspirin 81 mg oral tablets. # Keep the first treatment episode for each person. cdm$treated <- conceptCohort(   cdm = cdm,   conceptSet = list(treated = 19059056L),   name = "treated" ) |>   requireIsFirstEntry() #> ℹ Subsetting table drug_exposure using 1 concept with domain: drug. #> ℹ Combining tables. #> ℹ Creating cohort attributes. #> ℹ Applying cohort requirements. #> ℹ Merging overlapping records. #> ✔ Cohort treated created.  # Enter the untreated state the day after treatment ends. Require that day # to be within observation, so loss to follow-up is not a discontinuation. cdm$untreated <- cdm$treated |>   padCohortEnd(days = 1L, requireFullContribution = TRUE, name = "untreated") |>   padCohortDate(     days = 0L,     indexDate = "cohort_end_date",     cohortDate = "cohort_start_date"   ) |>   renameCohort("untreated") cdm <- bind(cdm$treated, cdm$untreated, name = "states")  # Model first discontinuation: untreated is an absorbing state. # Matrix state names must match the cohort names. trans <- transMat(   x = list(2, integer()),   names = c("treated", "untreated") )  # Estimate probabilities during the first year, overall and by initial state. result <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(   cohort = cdm$states,   trans = trans,   followUpDays = 365,   stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated") ) tidy(result) |>   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   cdm_name initial_state variable_name  variable_level probability #>   <chr>    <chr>         <chr>          <chr>                <dbl> #> 1 GiBleed  overall       prob_treated   0                    1     #> 2 GiBleed  overall       prob_untreated 0                    0     #> 3 GiBleed  overall       prob_treated   15                   0.320 #> 4 GiBleed  overall       prob_untreated 15                   0.680 #> 5 GiBleed  overall       prob_treated   16                   0.319 #> 6 GiBleed  overall       prob_untreated 16                   0.681 #> # ℹ 5 more variables: cohort_table_name <chr>, follow_up_days <chr>, #> #   state_hierarchy <chr>, state_step <chr>, transitions <chr>  # Sex is constant within each person and can be used for stratification. cdm$states <- PatientProfiles::addSex(cdm$states) bySex <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(   cohort = cdm$states,   trans = trans,   strata = list("sex"),   followUpDays = 365,   stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated") ) #> `cohort_table_name` eliminated from settings as all elements are NA. bySex |>   filterGroup(initial_state == "treated") |>   filterStrata(sex == "Female") |>   tidy() |>   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   cdm_name initial_state sex    variable_name  variable_level probability #>   <chr>    <chr>         <chr>  <chr>          <chr>                <dbl> #> 1 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_treated   0                    1     #> 2 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_untreated 0                    0     #> 3 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_treated   15                   0.305 #> 4 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_untreated 15                   0.695 #> 5 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_treated   22                   0.208 #> 6 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_untreated 22                   0.792 #> # ℹ 4 more variables: follow_up_days <chr>, state_hierarchy <chr>, #> #   state_step <chr>, transitions <chr>  cdmDisconnect(cdm)
